alert_name: Suspicious PowerShell Execution — Obfuscation or Anomalous Parent
escalation_condition: Critical if 4104 Script Block contains download cradle or network socket pattern, OR if child processes indicate active domain enumeration

related_techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
related_techniques.relevance: Encoded commands obscure payload from command-line logging

related_techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
related_techniques.relevance: Download cradles fetch second-stage payloads into memory

related_techniques.name: Account Discovery
related_techniques.relevance: net user /domain child process from PowerShell

related_techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
related_techniques.relevance: ipconfig, arp child processes from PowerShell

description: Detects adversary abuse of PowerShell through three complementary signals: (A) PowerShell spawned by a high-risk parent process such as an Office application or script host; (B) PowerShell executed with an obfuscation flag combination (encoded command, execution policy bypass, hidden window) scoring above threshold; (C) PowerShell spawning discovery or staging child processes consistent with post-exploitation enumeration.

variants.name: Suspicious Parent Process
variants.description: powershell.exe or pwsh.exe spawned by an Office application, browser, or script host with no legitimate reason to invoke a scripting engine.
variants.threshold: Any single instance of WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE, OUTLOOK.EXE, mshta.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, or regsvr32.exe as parent of powershell.exe.

variants.name: Obfuscation Flag Combination
variants.description: powershell.exe command line contains multiple evasion flags that together indicate intent to hide execution.
variants.threshold: Flag score >= 4 using the weighted scoring in detection.md: -EncodedCommand (+3), -ExecutionPolicy Bypass (+2), -WindowStyle Hidden (+2), -NonInteractive (+1), -NoProfile (+1).

variants.name: Suspicious Child Processes
variants.description: powershell.exe spawns 2 or more discovery or staging binaries within a short time window.
variants.threshold: ChildCount >= 2 of {whoami, net.exe, nltest, ipconfig, ping, certutil, bitsadmin, wmic, vssadmin, bcdedit, schtasks, reg.exe} from the same parent PowerShell PID within 5 minutes.

required_fields.description: Full path of the spawned process. Must match powershell.exe or pwsh.exe for Variants A and B; any discovery binary for Variant C.
Full path of the parent process. Used to classify the parent as suspicious (Variant A) or as powershell.exe (Variant C).
Full command line of the spawned process. Required for flag scoring (Variant B) and child process classification (Variant C). Requires command-line auditing enabled in GPO.
Full command line of the parent process. Required to correlate the spawning context for Variants A and B.
The user account under which the process ran. Used for privilege context (SYSTEM vs standard user) and anomaly detection (service account running interactive PowerShell).
Process integrity level (Low, Medium, High, System). High integrity for a standard user is anomalous and escalates severity.
Process creation time. Used for time-of-day anomaly detection and multi-event correlation.
Decoded PowerShell script content. Optional but high-fidelity — reveals encoded payload, download cradles, and AMSI bypass attempts.

enrichment_steps: Decode the -EncodedCommand value (base64 UTF-16LE decode) and inspect the plaintext. Look for IEX, DownloadString, WebClient, TCPClient, or Reflection.Assembly.
Correlate ProcessId from 4688 with EventID 4104 ScriptBlockId to retrieve decoded script content if Script Block Logging is enabled.
Check for Sysmon EventID 3 (Network Connection) from the same ProcessId — outbound connections from powershell.exe direct to IPs (not hostnames) are a strong download-cradle indicator.
Review the full process tree: what spawned the parent, and what did PowerShell subsequently spawn?
For Scenario B (svchost parent): identify the scheduled task name by querying EventID 4698 (scheduled task creation) or examining Task Scheduler logs around the same timestamp.
Check SubjectUser privilege level: a service account (svc_account1) running interactive PowerShell with High integrity outside business hours is a critical escalation signal.

recommended_actions.action: Isolate the host if active download or C2 connection is confirmed
recommended_actions.detail: If Sysmon EventID 3 shows an outbound connection from powershell.exe, or 4104 contains a network socket or download cradle, immediately isolate WORKSTATION-01 via EDR network isolation to prevent data exfiltration or further payload staging.
Terminate the identified powershell.exe PID via EDR. Do not simply close the window — terminate by PID to prevent the process from completing its payload if still running.
Before remediation: acquire process memory dump of the PowerShell PID, collect the 4104 script block text, export Sysmon and Security event logs for the host for the incident window.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate the parent process and delivery vector
recommended_actions.detail: For Scenario A: identify the source document (Q4_Bonus_Statement.docm) — retrieve from quarantine or user's Downloads folder. For Scenario B: enumerate all scheduled tasks on the host and identify the task that triggered svchost to spawn PowerShell at 02:47.

recommended_actions.action: Review affected user account and service account
recommended_actions.detail: For LAB\user1 (Scenario A): check for credential exposure — was the payload a stealer? For LAB\svc_account1 (Scenario B): audit all logon events, check for new scheduled tasks, services, or registry run keys created under this account.

false_positive_notes: Common benign triggers: SCCM/Intune agent deployments (parent: CCMExec.exe, user: SYSTEM), RMM tools (ConnectWise, Kaseya), developer build toolchains (node.exe, cargo.exe), IT admin scripts using -ep bypass for legitimate deployment. See detection.md for full guidance and allowlist templates.
